newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli secret police win right to use force.
newsitem.headline: Israeli secret police win right to use force.

text.p: Israel's High Court overturned on Thursday an interim court order which had forbidden Israel's Shin Bet secret police using "physical force" against a Palestinian detainee, a courts spokesman said.
"There is no justification to continue the interim order," court spokesman Moshe Gorali said, quoting the decision.
"This essentially means that they are allowing the security services to use the necessary force to get the information they need to advance the investigation," Gorali added.

Israeli media reports said the detainee, Muhammad Abdel Aziz Khamdan from Beit Sira village in the West Bank, was a member of the militant Islamic Jihad group and had information about attacks planned against Israeli targets.
"Yesterday the court issued an interim order preventing the use of physical pressure against the suspect after he appealed that he had been subjected to torture," Gorali said.

A 1987 Israeli commission ruled the Shin Bet could use "moderate physical pressure" in interrogations and "increased physical pressure" when an attack was imminent. Human rights groups have said the commission's report sanctioned torture.
Gorali had said the emergency appeal was intended to allow investigators to continue to use physical force to extract information from the detainee.

"I have no doubt that this could be connected to (suicide) attacks that were conducted in the past or to a planned attack in the future. We must therefore allow the security services to do their work," former Shin Bet chief Yaacov Perry told Israel radio. Perry said he had no details about Hamdan's case.

Israel has been on high alert for a possible Islamic Jihad suicide attack to mark the anniversary of the assassination of the group's leader, Fathi Shqaqi, in Malta last year. Shqaqi's killers were never caught but Palestinians blame Israel.
The Islamic Jihad has claimed responsibility for suicide attacks in Israel which left scores of people dead.
